summary: Continuation of RD.3 (overconvergent isocrystals and frames) after the accepted main packet PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology.json, whose RD.3 nodes it cites by id and does not repeat. It plans the open items of the main coverage record from Berthelot's public preprint IRMAR 96-03, which contains the proofs the main pass treated as unpublished: the étale tube isomorphism and the étale strict-neighbourhood theorem behind the weak and strong fibration theorems; the j† calculus, coherent j†O-modules as germs on strict neighbourhoods, and their gluing; overconvergence as a property with Berthelot's coordinate criterion; the gluing construction of isocrystals without a global frame and the Zariski stack property; the Monsky–Washnitzer description of overconvergent isocrystals on a smooth affine and the Dwork–Berthelot theorem that a Frobenius structure forces overconvergence. It owns the ordinary convergent coefficient model: convergent isocrystals and F-isocrystals, Dwork's construction of the convergent F-isocrystal of an F-crystal and Berthelot–Ogus's comparison with crystals up to isogeny, the underlying bundle on a ramified smooth formal scheme (Guo–Reinecke), unit-root F-isocrystals and the Katz–Crew correspondence with lisse ℚ_q-sheaves. From Étesse it plans the henselian property of weak completions with Elkik's descent of projective modules, the lifting of étale algebras, the overconvergence of convergent direct summands and étale descent for overconvergent F-isocrystals; the finite étale pushforward (formerly Tsuzuki 2002) is constructed from these. It replaces Abe's unread counterexample by an explicit extension of the unit by a Kummer isocrystal with a p-adic Liouville-type exponent, showing that restriction from overconvergent to convergent isocrystals is not full without Frobenius. Proofs and corrections for 19 main-packet nodes are recorded as continuations; Étesse's abelian-scheme theorem and Berthelot–Tsuzuki relative overconvergence are proposed for RD.5.

nodes.title: Étale maps induce isomorphisms of tubes
nodes.statement: Let X be a k-scheme of finite type, i: X → P and i′: X → P′ immersions into formal O-schemes of finite type, and u: P′ → P a morphism with u∘i′ = i which is étale on a neighbourhood of i′(X). Then u_K restricts to an isomorphism of rigid spaces ]X[_{P′} → ]X[_P. Moreover, for every closed tube radius λ ∈ |K^×|^ℚ with λ < 1 sufficiently close to 1, u_K restricts to an isomorphism of the closed tubes [X]_{P′,λ} → [X]_{P,λ}.
hypotheses: X need not be smooth; P and P′ need not be smooth; only étaleness of u near X is used.
The tube depends only on an open formal subscheme containing X, so P and P′ may be shrunk to opens containing X.
proofSteps: Replace P and P′ by opens containing X so that X is closed in both, u is étale and P′ ×_P X → X is an isomorphism (an étale map with a section is an open immersion near the section). Since tubes are local on P (the generic fibres of an affine covering form an admissible covering), assume P = Spf A and P′ = Spf A′ affine (Berthelot 96-03, proof of (1.3.1), p. 39).

Let f_1, …, f_r ∈ A lift equations of X modulo the maximal ideal of O and a ∈ m_K nonzero. The closed tube of radius λ = |a|^{1/n} is the affinoid with algebra A{T}/(f_i^n − aT_i) ⊗ K, and the same presentation with A′ describes [X]_{P′,λ} (Berthelot (1.1.9)). It therefore suffices that A[T]/(a^m, f_i^n − aT_i) → A′[T]/(a^m, f_i^n − aT_i) is an isomorphism for all m, n.

The ideal generated by the f_i in A[T]/(a^m, f_i^n − aT_i) is nilpotent; A′[T] is étale over A[T] and the two rings agree modulo that nilpotent ideal ((A/I)[T] ≅ (A′/IA′)[T]). An étale algebra which becomes an isomorphism modulo a nilpotent ideal is an isomorphism (formal étaleness), so each map is an isomorphism; passing to the limit over m gives the closed-tube statement, and the open tube is the admissible union of the closed tubes as λ → 1.
acceptance: Square root near 1: for p odd, P = P′ = Spf O⟨t, t^{-1}⟩ with u(t) = t² and X = {t = 1}: u is étale and u_K maps the residue disc {|t − 1| < 1} isomorphically onto {|s − 1| < 1}, the inverse being the binomial series of (1 + (s − 1))^{1/2}, whose coefficients are p-integral.

Non-example: for the projection P × Spf O⟨x⟩ → P with X embedded by the zero section, u is smooth but not étale, and the tube of X upstairs is the product of ]X[_P with an open unit disc, not isomorphic to ]X[_P.
With P′ = P and u the identity the statement is the identity of ]X[_P (degenerate case).

sources.match: States that an étale map compatible with the immersions induces an isomorphism of open tubes and of closed tubes of radius close to 1, proved by reducing to affine formal schemes and comparing the presentations of the closed tubes modulo powers of a.

nodes.title: Strict neighbourhoods: admissible-covering definition, criterion and standard systems
nodes.statement: Let P be a formal O-scheme of finite type, Y ⊆ P_k a closed subscheme, X ⊆ Y open and Z = Y ∖ X. For η ∈ |K^×|^ℚ, η < 1, put U_η = ]Y[_P ∖ ]Z[_{P,η}. (a) An admissible open V ⊆ ]Y[_P containing ]X[_P is a strict neighbourhood of ]X[_P (the covering (V, ]Z[_P) of ]Y[_P is admissible) if and only if for every affinoid W ⊆ ]Y[_P there is η_0 < 1 with W ∩ U_η ⊆ V for all η_0 ≤ η < 1; when P is affine and g_1, …, g_s ∈ Γ(P, O_P) cut out Z inside Y, U_η may be replaced by U′_η = {x ∈ ]Y[_P : max_j |g_j(x)| ≥ η}. (b) For increasing sequences λ_n → 1 and η_n → 1 in |K^×|^ℚ the union V_{λ,η} = ⋃_n ([Y]_{λ_n} ∩ U_{η_n}) is a strict neighbourhood, independent of the chosen equations after discarding finitely many terms, and for fixed λ the V_{λ,η} form a fundamental system; they are pseudo-compact in ]Y[_P. (c) Strict neighbourhoods are stable under finite intersection, are local on P, and pull back to strict neighbourhoods along morphisms of triples (X′, Y′, P′) → (X, Y, P); the complement in ]Y[_P of a closed analytic subspace of P_K missing ]X[_P is a strict neighbourhood. (d) If X is open in a larger closed Y′ ⊇ Y, an open V ⊇ ]X[ of ]Y[ is a strict neighbourhood in ]Y[ if and only if it is one in ]Y′[; for opens X_1, X_2 of Y with strict neighbourhoods V_1, V_2, V_1 ∩ V_2 is a strict neighbourhood of ]X_1 ∩ X_2[ and, when V_1, V_2 are pseudo-compact, V_1 ∪ V_2 is one of ]X_1 ∪ X_2[ with (V_1, V_2) an admissible covering.
hypotheses: The covering (]X[, ]Z[) of ]Y[ is not admissible in general, which is why strict neighbourhoods are needed (Berthelot's remark after (1.2.1)).
Radii are taken in |K^×|^ℚ so that the tubes and the sets U_η are finite unions of rational domains.
proofSteps: (a): if V is strict, the admissible covering (V, ]Z[_η)_{η→1} of W has a finite subcovering, so some U_η ∩ W lies in V; conversely, for P affine, for any affinoid h: Spm B → ]Y[ the maximum principle puts the image in some [Y]_λ, and the finitely many special domains [Z]_η and {|g_i| ≥ η} ∩ [Y]_λ refine (V, ]Z[) (Berthelot 96-03 (1.2.2), p. 33). The replacement of U_η by U′_η uses the maximum principle once more on W (1.2.3)(iii).

(b): the V_{λ,η} are open with the indicated special covering, and given any strict V′, quasi-compactness of [Y]_{λ_n} and (a) produce η_n with U_{η_n} ∩ [Y]_{λ_n} ⊆ V′ (1.2.4)(i); pseudo-compactness is (1.2.9).

(c): intersections and locality are immediate from the admissible-covering definition and (1.2.3)(ii); pullback is (1.2.7), using v^{-1}(Z) ⊆ Z′; complements of closed analytic subspaces are (1.2.4)(ii) by the maximum principle.
(d): (1.2.11) uses the admissible covering (]Y[, ]Z′[) of ]Y′[ ((1.1.14)(ii)); the intersection and union statements are (1.2.10).
acceptance: Affine space: for P the formal projective space over O and X = A^n_k ⊂ P^n_k = Y, the sets U_η are the closed balls of radius 1/η around 0, so the closed balls of radius > 1 form a fundamental system of strict neighbourhoods of the closed unit polydisc (Berthelot (1.2.4)(iii)).

Non-example: for P = Spf O⟨t⟩, Y = A^1_k and Z the origin, ]X[ is the annulus |t| = 1 and ]X[ itself is not a strict neighbourhood: the covering (]X[, ]Z[) of the closed disc is not admissible by the maximum principle.
If Z = ∅ (X = Y) every admissible open containing ]X[ is a strict neighbourhood, in particular ]X[ itself.

sources.match: Defines strict neighbourhoods by admissibility of the covering (V, ]Z[), proves the affinoid criterion, the standard neighbourhoods V_{λ,η} with their independence of equations, pullback along morphisms of triples, and the behaviour under intersections, unions and enlargement of Y.

nodes.title: Étale morphisms proper over the closure of X induce isomorphisms of strict neighbourhoods
nodes.statement: Let X ⊆ Y be an open immersion of k-schemes of finite type, i: Y → P and i′: Y′ → P′ closed immersions into formal O-schemes of finite type, v: Y′ → Y and u: P′ → P morphisms with u∘i′ = i∘v and v restricting to the identity on X ⊆ Y′ (X open in Y′). Let X̄ be the closure of X in P′ ×_P Y. If u is étale on a neighbourhood of X and the restriction of v to X̄ is proper, then u_K induces an isomorphism from a strict neighbourhood of ]X[_{P′} in ]Y′[_{P′} onto a strict neighbourhood of ]X[_P in ]Y[_P.
hypotheses: Properness of v on the closure of X is essential: it is used to show that the closure of the relevant analytic domain is finite over P_K.
The étaleness of u is required only near X; P and P′ may be singular along Y ∖ X and Y′ ∖ X.
proofSteps: Reduce to v proper with v^{-1}(X) = X by replacing Y′ with X̄ (standard-strict-neighbourhoods (d)); localise on a finite affine covering of P, and on a finite covering of X, so that P = Spf A, X = D(g) ∩ Y, and the standard neighbourhoods are built from U_η = {|g| ≥ η}; after the base change P_1 = Spf A{T}/(f_i^q − aT_i) one may assume [Y]_λ = P_K (Berthelot 96-03, proof of (1.3.5), pp. 42–43).

Write P′ ×_P Y = Y′ ⊔ D with X open and closed in P′ ×_P X (u étale with a section over X). Choose μ < 1 with P′_K ∖ ]Y′[ ⊆ [D]_μ and then λ_0 < 1 with P′_K ∖ ]D[_μ ⊆ [Y′]_{λ_0}; by the maximum principle, for each λ ≥ λ_0 there is η < 1 with [Y′]_λ ∩ [D]_μ ∩ U′_η = ∅, so T_K = [Y′]_λ ∩ U′_η is open and closed, hence a closed analytic subspace of U′_η.

By the Jacobian criterion the non-smooth and non-étale loci of T_K → P_K are closed analytic subsets missing ]X[_{P′} (where etale-tube-isomorphism applies), so after enlarging η the map T_K → U_η is étale; after one more base change T_K is closed in P′_K, its schematic closure T in P′ has special fibre inside Y′, hence is proper over P because v is proper.

By the comparison of formal and rigid properness T_K → P_K is proper, hence finite since it is étale (quasi-finite and proper implies finite), given by a coherent O_{P_K}-algebra 𝓇. The map O_{P_K} → 𝓇 is an isomorphism over ]X[_P, and its kernel and cokernel are supported on closed analytic subsets missing ]X[_P, so it is an isomorphism over U_η for η close to 1; thus T_K ∩ U′_η → U_η is an isomorphism, which gives the required strict neighbourhoods.
acceptance: Degenerate case: Y′ = Y and u = id give the identity on any strict neighbourhood.
Open immersion: if u is the inclusion of an open formal subscheme P′ ⊆ P containing Y and Y′ = Y, the strict neighbourhoods of ]X[ in ]Y[_{P′} and in ]Y[_P coincide.

Non-example showing properness is needed: P = Spf O⟨t⟩, Y = A^1_k, X = G_m = Y ∖ {0}, P′ = Spf O⟨t, t^{-1}⟩ the open formal subscheme over X, Y′ = X and v the inclusion, which is not proper. Then ]Y′[_{P′} = {|t| = 1} = ]X[_P, which is not a strict neighbourhood of ]X[_P in the closed unit disc ]Y[_P, because the covering of the closed disc by the annulus |t| = 1 and the open disc |t| < 1 is not admissible.

sources.match: States and proves that an étale morphism of formal schemes, proper on the closure of X, induces an isomorphism between strict neighbourhoods of the tubes of X, by isolating an open and closed analytic domain, proving it étale over P_K by the Jacobian criterion and maximum principle, and finite via Raynaud's properness comparison.

Restates the result in the language of V-triples (étale around Y, proper, isomorphism on X) and deduces that pullback of coherent j†-modules is an equivalence with quasi-inverse the direct image, citing Berthelot's Théorème 1.3.5.

nodes.title: j† is exact, commutes with tensor products, is functorial and localises on X
nodes.statement: In the setting of RD.3/j-dagger, let V be a strict neighbourhood of ]X[_P in ]Y[_P and 𝒜 a sheaf of rings on V. (a) For every 𝒜-module E the canonical map E → j†E is an epimorphism, an isomorphism when E is a j†𝒜-module, and E ⊗_𝒜 j†𝒜 → j†E is an isomorphism; j† is exact on 𝒜-modules, its restriction to ]X[ is the identity and its restriction to V ∩ ]Z[ is zero; Γ(]Y[, E) → Γ(V, E) is bijective for j†𝒜-modules E. (b) For a morphism of triples (w, v, u): (X′, Y′, P′) → (X, Y, P) and strict neighbourhoods with u_K(V′) ⊆ V there are canonical maps j†E → u_{K*} j′† u_K^{-1}E and, for modules, j†E → u_{K*} j′† u_K^*E; when X′ = v^{-1}(X) the maps u_K^{-1} j†E → j′† u_K^{-1}E and u_K^* j†E → j′† u_K^* E are isomorphisms. (c) For E coherent on V the map j†E → j_{K*} j_K^* E to the sections on ]X[ is injective. (d) For a finite open covering X = X_1 ∪ … ∪ X_n with inclusions j_{i_0…i_k} of the intersections, the alternating Čech complex 0 → j†E → ⊕ j_{i}†E → ⊕_{i_0<i_1} j_{i_0 i_1}†E → … is exact; equivalently j_1† j_2† ≅ j†_{X_1 ∩ X_2} and the sections supported in ]Z[ satisfy Γ_{]Z_1[} Γ_{]Z_2[} = Γ_{]Z_1 ∩ Z_2[}.
hypotheses: No coherence is needed for (a), (b) and (d); (c) needs E coherent on a strict neighbourhood.
The isomorphism statements in (b) need X′ = v^{-1}(X); without it only the canonical maps exist.
proofSteps: (a): sections of j†E over a quasi-compact W are germs of sections over W ∩ V′, V′ strict; surjectivity of E → j†E is local and follows by covering W by the special domains {|t_i| ≥ η} and [Z]_{η′}, on the latter the germ lifting to zero; injectivity for j†𝒜-modules uses that (U_η, ]Z[) covers V admissibly and that j†-modules vanish on ]Z[; the tensor formula follows from the universal property and exactness from exactness of filtered colimits and the epimorphism (Berthelot 96-03 (2.1.1)–(2.1.3), pp. 47–51).

(b): the maps come from pulling back germs of sections along u_K, using that preimages of strict neighbourhoods are strict (standard-strict-neighbourhoods (c)); when X′ = v^{-1}(X) an explicit inverse is constructed on affine charts from the sets U_η and U′_η = u_K^{-1}(U_η) ∩ ]Y′[ ((2.1.4), pp. 51–53).
(c): a section killed on ]X[ has support a closed analytic, hence quasi-compact, subset of a quasi-compact W disjoint from ]X[, so it is contained in some [Z]_η and the germ is zero ((2.1.5), p. 53).

(d): for two opens, compute the germs over V_1 ∩ V_2 and use that the products g′_i g″_j define Z_1 ∪ Z_2 ((2.1.7)); the general exactness follows by induction on n from the exact sequences 0 → Γ_{]Z[} → id → j† → 0 ((2.1.6), (2.1.8), pp. 53–56).
acceptance: Affine space: for P the formal projective n-space and X = A^n_k, Γ(P_K, j†O) is the ring K⟨t_1, …, t_n⟩† of series with radius of convergence > 1 (Berthelot (2.1.2.3)), while Γ(]X[, j†O) = K⟨t_1, …, t_n⟩, so j† genuinely changes global sections.
Degenerate case: if Z = ∅ then j†E = E.
Two-open covering of G_m = A^1 ∖ {0} ⊂ P^1 by A^1 ∖ {0} itself and a second copy: the Čech sequence of (d) reduces to j†E ≅ j†E.

sources.match: Defines the sheaf of overconvergent germs, proves exactness, the tensor formula, functoriality for morphisms of triples with the isomorphism criterion X′ = v^{-1}(X), injectivity into sections on the tube for coherent sheaves, and the Čech/Mayer–Vietoris resolution localising j† on X.
Re-proves these properties of j† for V-triples, with references to Berthelot's numbering.

nodes.title: Coherent j†O-modules are germs of coherent modules on strict neighbourhoods
nodes.statement: In the setting of RD.3/j-dagger: (a) j†O_{]Y[} is a coherent sheaf of rings, and coherent j†O_{]Y[}-modules form an abelian subcategory of all j†O_{]Y[}-modules stable under ⊗ and internal Hom. (b) Every coherent j†O_{]Y[}-module is isomorphic to j†𝓮 for a coherent O_V-module 𝓮 on some strict neighbourhood V, and for coherent 𝓮, 𝓯 on V, Hom(j†𝓮, j†𝓯) = colim_{V′ ⊆ V} Hom_{O_{V′}}(𝓮|_{V′}, 𝓯|_{V′}); thus the category of coherent j†O-modules is the 2-colimit over strict neighbourhoods of the categories of coherent modules, and E is locally free of finite rank if and only if it is j†𝓮 for a locally free 𝓮. (c) The restriction functor from coherent j†O_{]Y[}-modules to coherent O_{]X[}-modules is exact and faithful.
hypotheses: The 2-colimit in (b) is over the filtered set of strict neighbourhoods; two coherent modules on strict neighbourhoods define the same germ if they become isomorphic on a smaller strict neighbourhood.
proofSteps: (a): finite generation of kernels of maps (j†O)^n → j†O is checked on an admissible affinoid covering; on W ∩ ]Z[ the kernel vanishes and on W ∩ V it is j† of the kernel of a map of coherent O-modules, by exactness of j† (j-dagger-exactness-and-functoriality (a)) (Berthelot 96-03 (2.1.9), p. 56).

(b): first, for each λ < 1, find η and coherent models on V_λ = U_η ∩ [Y]_λ, using that [Y]_λ is quasi-compact and that on affinoids with finite presentations the statement reduces to E = j†O (formula (2.1.1.5)); then build compatible models on ⋃_{n' ≤ n} V_{n'} by induction along sequences λ_n, η_n → 1 and glue on the standard strict neighbourhood V_{λ,η}, which the V_n cover admissibly; the Hom statement is proved the same way ((2.1.10), pp. 56–57, and the remark after it).

(c): a morphism f = j†(g) vanishing on ]X[ has image supported on a closed analytic subset missing ]X[, which a smaller strict neighbourhood avoids ((2.1.11), p. 57); exactness is that of restriction to an open.
acceptance: Affine space: the coherent j†O-modules on P^n_K for X = A^n_k correspond to finitely generated K⟨t⟩†-modules (Berthelot (2.5.2)(i) with A = O[t]).

Faithful but not full: on the frame (A^1_k, P^1_k, P̂^1), the injection K⟨t⟩† → K⟨t⟩ is the restriction functor on global sections of the free rank-one module; the element Σ p^{⌊√n⌋} t^n of K⟨t⟩ shows Hom(j†O, j†O) = K⟨t⟩† is a proper subspace of Hom(O_{]X[}, O_{]X[}) = K⟨t⟩.
Degenerate case: if Z = ∅, coherent j†O-modules are coherent O_{]Y[}-modules.

sources.match: Proves coherence of j†O, the description of coherent j†O-modules (and of locally free ones) as germs of coherent modules on strict neighbourhoods with the colimit formula for Hom, and faithfulness of restriction to the tube.
Records exactness and faithfulness of restriction to the tube for coherent j†-modules, citing Berthelot (2.1.11).

nodes.title: Coherent j†O-modules glue along finite open coverings of X
nodes.statement: Let X = X_1 ∪ … ∪ X_n be a finite open covering, j_i: X_i → Y the inclusions and j_i† the corresponding functors on ]Y[_P. (a) Given coherent (respectively locally free of finite rank) j_i†O_{]Y[}-modules E_i and isomorphisms j_{i′}†E_i ≅ j_i†E_{i′} satisfying the cocycle condition, there is a coherent (respectively locally free) j†O_{]Y[}-module E, unique up to unique isomorphism, with isomorphisms j_i†E ≅ E_i compatible with the given ones. (b) Given coherent E, F and maps φ_i: j_i†E → j_i†F with j_{i′}†φ_i = j_i†φ_{i′}, there is a unique φ: E → F with j_i†φ = φ_i. Hence X′ ↦ {coherent j_{X′}†O_{]Y[}-modules} is a stack for the Zariski topology on X (Y and P fixed).
hypotheses: The covering is finite; for a general Zariski covering of a quasi-compact X refine to a finite one.
proofSteps: By coherent-j-dagger-modules (b) each E_i is j_i†𝓮_i for a coherent 𝓮_i on a strict neighbourhood V_i of ]X_i[, and the gluing isomorphisms come from isomorphisms of models on strict neighbourhoods of ]X_i ∩ X_{i′}[ (Berthelot 96-03 (2.1.12), p. 58).

Shrink the V_i to standard neighbourhoods V^i_{λ,η} for a common pair of sequences; their union is the standard neighbourhood of ]X[ and they form an admissible covering of it (standard-strict-neighbourhoods (b), (d)); after shrinking once more the isomorphisms satisfy the cocycle condition on triple overlaps, so the 𝓮_i glue to a coherent 𝓮 on V and E = j†𝓮 works; uniqueness and (b) follow from the Hom formula and the Čech sequence of j-dagger-exactness-and-functoriality (d).
acceptance: Covering G_m ⊂ P^1 by the two opens obtained by removing 1 and −1 (p odd): a locally free module given on each piece and agreeing on the overlap glues to a locally free j†O-module.
Degenerate case n = 1: the gluing datum is a single module and E = E_1.
Morphisms: the identity maps on the pieces glue to the identity of E (uniqueness in (b)).

sources.match: Proves that coherent and locally free j†O-modules, and their morphisms, glue along finite open coverings of X, so that they form a stack on Y in the X variable.

nodes.title: Overconvergence of a connection is a property, local on P and on X, stable under subquotients
nodes.statement: Let (X, Y, P) be as in RD.3/j-dagger with a morphism P → S of formal O-schemes smooth on a neighbourhood of X, and let E be a coherent j†O_{]Y[}-module with an integrable connection ∇ relative to S_K. (a) (E, ∇) ≅ j†(𝓮, ∇_0) for a coherent O_V-module 𝓮 with integrable connection on some strict neighbourhood V; if S = Spf O then E is locally free of finite rank. (b) ∇ is overconvergent along Z = Y ∖ X — there is an isomorphism ε: p_2^*E ≅ p_1^*E of j†O_{]Y[_{P×_S P}}-modules inducing the Taylor isomorphisms ε_n modulo the (n+1)-st power of the diagonal ideal for all n — if and only if there is an isomorphism ε′: p_2^*𝓮 ≅ p_1^*𝓮 on a strict neighbourhood of ]X[_{P×P} in ]Y[_{P×P} inducing the Taylor isomorphisms of ∇_0. (c) If ∇ is overconvergent, ε is unique, is determined by its restriction to ]X[_{P×P}, and satisfies the cocycle condition on ]Y[_{P×P×P}; a j†O-linear map h: E → F between overconvergent modules is compatible with the ε if and only if h|_{]X[} is horizontal; a section s satisfies ε(p_2^*s) = p_1^*s if and only if s|_{]X[} is horizontal; coherent sub-j†O-modules stable under ∇ and the corresponding quotients are again overconvergent. (d) Overconvergence can be tested on an open covering of P and on a finite open covering of X. (e) Coherent j†O-modules with integrable overconvergent connection form an abelian category with ⊗ and internal Hom, the forgetful functor to coherent j†O-modules is exact, the category is a full subcategory of coherent j†O-modules with integrable connection, and restriction to ]X[ is an exact faithful functor to coherent O_{]X[}-modules with convergent integrable connection.
hypotheses: K has characteristic 0 (needed for (a) and for the description of connections by divided-power Taylor series).
P → S is smooth only near X; by RD.3/j-dagger and the Jacobian criterion the smooth locus of P_K → S_K is a strict neighbourhood of ]X[.
proofSteps: (a): apply coherent-j-dagger-modules (b) to E and to the Taylor isomorphisms on the first-order neighbourhoods in the double and triple products; local freeness of a coherent module with connection in characteristic 0 is the classical argument (Berthelot 96-03 (2.2.3), p. 60).

(b): if ε′ exists, ε = j′†(ε′) using that j† commutes with the projections and the diagonal (j-dagger-exactness-and-functoriality (b)); conversely write ε = j′†(ε′) on a standard strict neighbourhood and show that ε′ induces the Taylor isomorphisms after shrinking: the kernel of restriction to ]X[ of sections of 𝓮 has support a closed analytic subset missing ]X[, avoided by U_η for η near 1 ((2.2.6), pp. 61–62).

(c): by faithfulness of restriction to the tube (coherent-j-dagger-modules (c)) reduce to Y = X; cover the closed tubes [X]_{P²,λ} by products W × D(0, λ^+)^m (weak fibration theorem, RD.3/weak-fibration-theorem), and use injectivity of M ⊗_A A{τ} → M ⊗_A A[[τ]] to see that ε is determined by its Taylor expansion; subobjects use flatness of the projections on the smooth locus, a strict neighbourhood ((2.2.1), pp. 58–59; (2.2.7), pp. 62–63).

(d): ε's obtained on an open covering of P glue by uniqueness ((2.2.8), p. 63); for a finite covering of X apply coherent-j-dagger-gluing (b) to the maps p_2^*E → p_1^*E ((2.2.11), pp. 63–64). (e) follows from (c), coherent-j-dagger-modules (a) and (c) ((2.2.9), (2.2.10), p. 63).
acceptance: Dwork: on (A^1_k, P^1_k, P̂^1_O) with K = ℚ_p(π), π^{p−1} = −p, the module j†O with ∇(1) = −π dt is overconvergent: its Taylor isomorphism is multiplication by exp(−π(t′ − t)), analytic on the strict neighbourhood |t′ − t| < 1 of the diagonal tube (Berthelot (2.2.15)(ii)(a), (1.2.4)(iv)).
Non-example: j†O with ∇(1) = −dt on the same frame is not overconvergent, not even convergent: its Taylor series exp(−(t′ − t)) converges only for |t′ − t| < p^{−1/(p−1)} < 1.
Subobjects: the image of a horizontal map between overconvergent modules is overconvergent by (c), so the category is abelian.

sources.match: Defines overconvergent connections by the existence of the global Taylor isomorphism on the tube of Y in P×P, shows it is a property (unique, determined on the tube of X), local on P and on X, inherited by sub- and quotient objects, and that the category is abelian with ⊗ and internal Hom and a full subcategory of modules with connection.

nodes.title: The coordinate criterion for convergence and overconvergence of a connection
nodes.statement: Assume P and S affine, Z = Y ∩ V(g) for one g ∈ Γ(P, O_P), and t_1, …, t_m ∈ Γ(P, O_P) such that dt_1, …, dt_m is a basis of Ω^1_{P/S} near X; on a strict neighbourhood of ]X[ these give a basis of Ω^1_{P_K/S_K} with dual derivations ∂_1, …, ∂_m. Let (𝓮, ∇_0) be a coherent module with integrable connection on a strict neighbourhood V and (E, ∇) = j†(𝓮, ∇_0); write ∂^{[k]} = ∂^k / k! for multi-indices k, and U_η = {x ∈ P_K : |g(x)| ≥ η}. Then ∇ is overconvergent if and only if for every λ < 1 in |K^×|^ℚ there is η < 1 in |K^×|^ℚ with [Y]_λ ∩ U_η ⊆ V such that ‖∂^{[k]} e‖ λ^{|k|} → 0 as |k| → ∞ for every e ∈ Γ([Y]_λ ∩ U_η, 𝓮), for a (any) Banach norm on this finite module over an affinoid algebra. When Z = ∅ (X closed in P), a connection on a coherent O_{]X[}-module is convergent if and only if ‖∂^{[k]} e‖ λ^{|k|} → 0 for every λ < 1 and every e ∈ Γ([X]_λ, 𝓮).
hypotheses: Divided powers ∂^k/k! need characteristic 0.
The criterion is coordinate-dependent in form but the conclusion is not; any other étale coordinates give the same answer (Guo–Reinecke, Remark 2.13).
proofSteps: Necessity: by overconvergence-is-a-property (b), ε = j′†(ε′) on a strict neighbourhood V′ ⊇ V_{λη} := [Y]_{P²,λ} ∩ p_1^{-1}(U_η); on [Y]_{P²,λ} the conditions |1 ⊗ g| ≥ η and |g ⊗ 1| ≥ η agree for η > λ. By Berthelot's remark (1.3.8)(ii) (strong fibration theorem applied to p_1), V_{λη} ≅ ([Y]_λ ∩ U_η) × D(0, λ^+)^m with coordinates τ_i = 1 ⊗ t_i − t_i ⊗ 1 (Berthelot 96-03 (2.2.13), pp. 64–65).

Expanding θ(e) = ε′(p_2^*e) = Σ_k θ_k(e) ⊗ τ^k with ‖θ_k(e)‖ λ^{|k|} → 0 (Lemma (2.2.12): finite modules over A{τ} expand uniquely in τ-series), compatibility of ε′ with the Taylor isomorphisms modulo the powers of the diagonal forces θ_k(e) = ∂^{[k]} e ((2.2.4.1)).

Sufficiency: for a sequence λ_i → 1 and corresponding η_i, define θ(e) = Σ_k ∂^{[k]} e ⊗ τ^k on V_{λ_i η_i}; it is semilinear, so gives a linear map p_2^*𝓮 → p_1^*𝓮 inducing the Taylor isomorphisms, with inverse Σ_k (−1)^{|k|} τ^k ⊗ ∂^{[k]} e; these glue by the uniqueness argument of overconvergence-is-a-property (c) to an isomorphism on the standard strict neighbourhood V_{λ,η} ((2.2.13)(ii), p. 66). The case Z = ∅ is (2.2.14).
acceptance: Dwork: for ∇(1) = −π dt on A^1 ⊂ P^1 (K = ℚ_p(π), π^{p−1} = −p), on the chart Spf O⟨t⟩, where Z is empty, ∂^{[k]}1 = (−π)^k/k! has absolute value p^{−s_p(k)/(p−1)} ≤ 1 (s_p the digit sum), so the connection is convergent there. Overconvergence along ∞ is checked on the chart Spf O⟨s⟩, s = 1/t, with g = s and U_η ∩ [Y]_λ = {η ≤ |s| ≤ 1}: there ∇(1) = π s^{−2} ds, the Taylor series of 1 is exp(π τ/(s(s + τ))) with τ = s′ − s, and expanding π τ/(s(s + τ)) = (π/s²) Σ_{j≥0} (−1)^j τ^{j+1}/s^j and using |π^n/n!| ≤ 1 gives ‖∂_s^{[k]}1‖ ≤ η^{−2k} on that annulus; so ‖∂_s^{[k]}1‖ λ^k → 0 once η² > λ, and the connection is overconvergent. Computing only on the chart at 0, where Z is empty, would test convergence and not overconvergence.
Kummer: for ∇(1) = a dt/t on G_m ⊂ P^1 with a ∈ ℤ_p, ∂^{[k]}1 = binom(a, k) t^{−k} with |binom(a, k)| ≤ 1, so on {η ≤ |t| ≤ 1/η} the norms are ≤ η^{−k} and λ^k η^{−k} → 0 for η > λ: overconvergent.

Non-examples: for ∇(1) = −dt, ‖∂^{[k]}1‖ = |1/k!| = p^{v_p(k!)} and λ^k p^{v_p(k!)} → ∞ for λ > p^{−1/(p−1)}; for a = 1/p in the Kummer example |binom(1/p, k)| = p^{k + v_p(k!)} is unbounded, so neither is even convergent.

sources.match: Proves that, in coordinates, overconvergence is equivalent to the decay of the divided-power derivatives of sections on the sets [Y]_λ ∩ U_η, and convergence to the same decay on the closed tubes [X]_λ; gives the Dwork and Kummer examples.

Uses the convergent case of the criterion (cited to Berthelot's Corollary 2.2.14) as the definition of a convergent connection on the generic fibre of an affine smooth formal scheme over W(k), and notes its independence of the coordinates.

nodes.title: Overconvergent isocrystals without a global frame: gluing, realisations and pullback
nodes.statement: Let X ⊆ Y be an open immersion of k-schemes of finite type over a formal O-scheme S of finite type. Choose a finite open covering (Y_α) of Y and closed immersions Y_α → P_α into formal S-schemes smooth near X_α = X ∩ Y_α; put Y_{αβ} = Y_α ∩ Y_β embedded diagonally in P_{αβ} = P_α ×_S P_β, with projections p_{αβ}, q_{αβ}. The category Isoc(X, Y/S) consists of families (E_α, φ_{αβ}) with E_α a coherent j†O_{]Y_α[}-module with integrable overconvergent connection and φ_{αβ}: p_{αβ,K}^* E_α ≅ q_{αβ,K}^* E_β horizontal isomorphisms on ]Y_{αβ}[_{P_{αβ}} satisfying the cocycle condition on ]Y_{αβγ}[_{P_α×P_β×P_γ}; morphisms are compatible families. (a) Up to canonical equivalence it does not depend on the covering or on the P_α, and equals Isoc(X, Y, P/S) when a global P exists. (b) For any immersion of an open U ⊆ Y into a formal S-scheme T (not necessarily smooth), each E has a realisation E_T on ]U[_T: locally E_T = u_K^* E_P for an S-morphism u: T → P to a smooth embedding of U restricting to the identity on U, independent of P and u up to canonical isomorphism, with canonical horizontal transition isomorphisms u_K^* E_T ≅ E_{T′} for S-morphisms u: T′ → T, satisfying transitivity. (c) For a commutative diagram (X′ ⊆ Y′ over S′) → (X ⊆ Y over S) given by v: Y′ → Y over S′ → S, there is a pullback functor v^*: Isoc(X, Y/S) → Isoc(X′, Y′/S′), realised by u_K^* for any lift u of v between embeddings, independent of u up to canonical isomorphism, with (v ∘ v′)^* ≅ v′^* ∘ v^* canonically.
hypotheses: Frames exist locally: every affine open of Y embeds as a closed subscheme of a formal affine space over S, which is smooth.

In (b) for O a discrete valuation ring, T may be any formal S-scheme in which U is defined by an ideal of definition (Berthelot (2.3.2)(ii), last paragraph): the lift u: T → P is built successively on the thickenings Spec O_T/𝓲^{i+1} by formal smoothness of P.
proofSteps: Independence of P on a fixed covering: two choices P_α, P′_α are compared through the diagonal embedding into P_α ×_S P′_α and the equivalences of RD.3/independence-of-frame along the two projections; the transition data match because the canonical isomorphisms of RD.3/taylor-comparison-of-pullbacks satisfy the transitivity relation (Berthelot 96-03 (2.2.17.3), (2.3.2)(i), pp. 67–70).

Independence of the covering (left to the reader by Berthelot, (2.3.2)(iii), p. 71; supplied here): given two coverings with embeddings, pass to the common refinement Y_α ∩ Y′_β embedded in P_α ×_S P′_β; restriction along the two projections gives equivalences from each gluing category to the refined one, because on each piece they are the equivalences of RD.3/independence-of-frame, and the cocycle data correspond since the Taylor isomorphism of an overconvergent module is unique (overconvergence-is-a-property (c)) and the comparison isomorphisms are transitive. Refining twice gives the compatibility needed for a canonical equivalence.

Realisations: choose locally a closed immersion of U into a smooth formal S-scheme P and lift U → P to u: T → P by formal smoothness on the nilpotent thickenings; set E_T = u_K^* E_P; two choices (P, u), (P′, u′) are compared through P ×_S P′ and RD.3/taylor-comparison-of-pullbacks, which yields independence and the transition isomorphisms ((2.3.2)(ii), (2.3.2.1), pp. 70–71).

Pullback: if v extends to u: P′ → P use u_K^*; otherwise replace P′ by P ×_S P′ with the graph embedding, whose projection to P extends v; canonicity again comes from RD.3/taylor-comparison-of-pullbacks ((2.3.2)(iv), pp. 71–72).
acceptance: Global frame: for Y = P^1_k covered by its two standard affine lines embedded in Â^1_O, and X = G_m, the gluing category is canonically equivalent to Isoc(G_m, P^1, P̂^1/K) defined with the global frame.

Cocycle condition matters: on a covering of Y by three opens, rank-one data with constant transition scalars c_{αβ} ∈ K^× whose product c_{αβ} c_{βγ} c_{γα} on the triple overlap is ≠ 1 do not define an object.

sources.match: Defines Isoc(X, Y/S) via a smooth embedding, the realisations E_T on arbitrary embeddings with transition isomorphisms, the gluing definition when no global embedding exists (independence of choices left to the reader), and the pullback functors with their compatibility with composition.

nodes.title: Overconvergent and convergent (F-)isocrystals form Zariski stacks
nodes.statement: (a) For fixed Y over S, the assignment of Isoc(X, Y/S) to each open X ⊆ Y, with restriction given by pullback, is a stack for the Zariski topology: for a finite open covering X = ⋃ X_i, objects of Isoc(X, Y/S) are equivalent to objects of the Isoc(X_i, Y/S) with gluing isomorphisms on the X_i ∩ X_j satisfying the cocycle condition, and morphisms glue uniquely. (b) The assignment X ↦ Isoc(X/S) of convergent isocrystals is a Zariski stack on X. (c) With a Frobenius lift σ on K, the same holds for the categories of overconvergent and convergent F^a-isocrystals. (d) Realisations, ⊗, internal Hom and pullback commute with restriction to opens.
hypotheses: Coverings are finite (Y quasi-compact); Zariski, not étale: étale descent is etale-descent-of-overconvergent-f-isocrystals and needs X smooth and Frobenius structures.
proofSteps: (a): overconvergence is local on X (overconvergence-is-a-property (d)) and coherent j†O-modules with their morphisms glue along finite coverings of X (coherent-j-dagger-gluing); apply this to the module and to the maps p_2^*E → p_1^*E (Berthelot 96-03, remark after (2.2.11), p. 64, and (2.3.3)(i), p. 72).
(b): for an open covering (X_α) of X the tubes ]X_α[ form an admissible covering of ]X[, so coherent modules with convergent connection glue ((2.3.3)(i)).
(c): Frobenius structures are isomorphisms in the stack and glue with the objects; Étesse uses this as the Zariski locality of F^a-Isoc†(X/K), citing Berthelot (2.1.12), (2.2.11), (2.3.7).
acceptance: Two opens: an overconvergent isocrystal on G_m ⊂ P^1 is the same as isocrystals on G_m ∖ {1} and G_m ∖ {−1} (p odd) with a gluing isomorphism on G_m ∖ {±1}.
Degenerate case: the trivial covering gives back Isoc(X, Y/S).
Boundary: the stack is in the X-variable with Y fixed; changing Y is governed by RD.3/independence-of-compactification.

sources.match: States that coherent j†O-modules with integrable overconvergent connection, and isocrystals overconvergent along Y − X, form a stack on Y in the variable X, and that convergent isocrystals form a stack because the tubes of an open covering form an admissible covering.
Records that F^a-Isoc†(X/K) is local for the Zariski topology on X, citing Berthelot (2.1.12), (2.2.11), (2.3.7).

nodes.title: On the Monsky–Washnitzer frame of a smooth affine, global sections give an equivalence with A†_K-modules
nodes.statement: Let X = Spec A_0 be a smooth affine k-scheme, A a smooth O-algebra lifting A_0 with a presentation A ≅ O[t_1, …, t_n]/I, 𝔛 = Spec A, P the formal completion of the closure of 𝔛 in P^n_O and Y its special fibre. Then ]Y[_P = P_K, the intersections U_η of 𝔛_K^an with the closed balls of radius 1/η > 1 form a fundamental system of affinoid strict neighbourhoods of ]X[_P, and Γ(P_K, j†O) = colim_η Γ(U_η, O) ≅ A† ⊗_O K =: A†_K, the generic fibre of the weak completion. The functor Γ(𝔛_K^an, −) = Γ(P_K, −) induces equivalences (i) from coherent j†O_{P_K}-modules to finitely generated A†_K-modules, locally free ones corresponding to projective ones; (ii) from coherent j†O-modules with integrable connection to finitely generated projective A†_K-modules M with integrable connection M → M ⊗_{A†_K} Ω^1_{A†_K} (Ω^1 in the sense of Monsky–Washnitzer); and (iii) from Isoc†(X/K) to those (M, ∇) whose Taylor series converges on a strict neighbourhood of the tube of the diagonal in 𝔛_K^an × 𝔛_K^an, for instance inside {|t_{2,i} − t_{1,i}| < 1 for all i}.
hypotheses: A smooth lift A exists (Elkik) and its weak completion is a dagger algebra of Monsky–Washnitzer type (AdicSpacesPartII:F1/mw-lift-existence-uniqueness).
Without Frobenius, the convergence condition in (iii) is genuine extra data (see the non-example).
proofSteps: The strict neighbourhoods: Berthelot 96-03 (1.2.4)(iii)–(iv) shows that in projective space the sets U_η = {x ∈ ]Y[ : |t_i(x)| ≤ 1/η} form a fundamental system; the restriction map from Γ(U_η, O) to Γ(]X[, O) = Â ⊗ K lands in A† ⊗ K by the growth description of A† (Berthelot (2.1.2.2)), and the colimit is A†_K ((2.1.2), (2.1.2.4), pp. 49–50).

(i): by coherent-j-dagger-modules (b) a coherent j†O-module is j†𝓮 with 𝓮 coherent on an affinoid U_η, i.e. a finite Γ(U_η, O)-module (Kiehl), and passing to the colimit gives a finite A†_K-module M = Γ(P_K, E) = Γ(U_η, E); locally free corresponds to projective ((2.5.2), pp. 82–83).

(ii): Γ(P_K, j†Ω^1) = colim Γ(U_η, Ω^1) = Ω^1_{A†} ⊗ K, so connections correspond, using overconvergence-is-a-property (a) for local freeness; (iii): overconvergence-is-a-property (b) with the explicit strict neighbourhood of the diagonal tube from (1.2.4)(iv) (remark after (2.5.2), p. 83).
acceptance: Affine space: for A = O[t_1, …, t_n], A†_K = K⟨t_1, …, t_n⟩†; the rank-one module with ∇(1) = −π dt_1 (Dwork) satisfies (iii).

Non-example: the A†_K-module A†_K with ∇(1) = −dt on A^1 is a projective module with integrable connection, so an object of (ii), but not of (iii): its Taylor series does not converge on |t_2 − t_1| < 1.
Degenerate case n = 0: X = Spec k, A†_K = K and both sides are finite-dimensional K-vector spaces.

sources.match: Identifies the overconvergent functions on the Monsky–Washnitzer frame with the weak completion, and proves that global sections give equivalences from coherent j†O-modules, modules with connection and overconvergent isocrystals to finitely generated (projective) A†_K-modules, with connection, whose Taylor series converges on a strict neighbourhood of the diagonal.

States the resulting equivalence between overconvergent F-isocrystals on a smooth affine and (σ,∇)-modules over the dagger algebra, attributing the automatic convergence to Berthelot's Théorème 2.5.7 (cited there as [Be4]).

nodes.title: Pullback along a lift of a morphism of smooth affines realises the pullback of overconvergent isocrystals
nodes.statement: Let w: X′ = Spec A′_0 → X = Spec A_0 be a morphism of smooth affine k-schemes, A, A′ smooth O-algebras lifting A_0, A′_0, and ψ: A† → A′† an O-algebra map between weak completions lifting w (it exists). Under the equivalences of affine-frame-global-sections-equivalence, the base-change functor ψ_K^* from A†_K-modules with integrable connection to A′†_K-modules with integrable connection preserves the convergence condition (iii), and its restriction to Isoc†(X/K) is canonically isomorphic to w^*: Isoc†(X/K) → Isoc†(X′/K). In particular two lifts ψ, ψ′ of w give canonically isomorphic functors, and the identification is compatible with composition. More generally, for immersions X → T, X′ → T′ into separated O-schemes of finite type smooth near X, X′, any morphism u′ from a strict neighbourhood of ]X′[_{T′} to T_K^an extending the map of tubes induced by a formal lift of w realises w^* on overconvergent isocrystals.
hypotheses: The lift ψ exists by the lifting property of weak completions (van der Put, Theorem 2.4.4; AdicSpacesPartII:F1/mw-morphism-lifting); it is not unique.
proofSteps: Bounds: for f ∈ A† and ρ > 1 there is η > 1 such that f extends to the affinoid U_η with sup norm ≤ ρ; hence ψ extends to morphisms U′_{η′} → U_η of strict neighbourhoods (Berthelot 96-03 (2.5.3), pp. 83–84).

A morphism u′ from a strict neighbourhood extending a map of tubes sends some strict neighbourhood into ]Y[ and pulls strict neighbourhoods back to strict neighbourhoods, by the maximum principle ((2.5.4), pp. 84–85).

Compare u′^* with w^* using the graph embedding X′ → P′ × P: u′ gives a section of the projection on a strict neighbourhood, and the projection induces an equivalence by RD.3/independence-of-compactification; composing shows that u′^* preserves overconvergence and is canonically isomorphic to w^* ((2.5.5)–(2.5.6), pp. 85–86).
acceptance: Frobenius: for a Frobenius lift F: A† → A† over σ, F_K^* realises the Frobenius pullback F^* on Isoc†(X/K); two Frobenius lifts give canonically isomorphic functors through the Taylor series of RD.0/change-of-frobenius-lift-taylor-formula.

nodes.title: Dwork–Berthelot: a Frobenius structure forces overconvergence
nodes.statement: In the setting of affine-frame-global-sections-equivalence, let σ be an automorphism of O lifting a power of the Frobenius of k, F: A† → A† a lift of the corresponding Frobenius of A_0 over σ, and (M, ∇) a finitely generated A†_K-module with integrable connection admitting a horizontal isomorphism Φ: (F^*M, F^*∇) ≅ (M, ∇). Then the coherent j†O-module with connection corresponding to (M, ∇) is overconvergent. Consequently (Berthelot's Corollary 2.5.8) the category of overconvergent F-isocrystals on X is equivalent to the category of finitely generated (necessarily projective) A†_K-modules with integrable connection and horizontal Frobenius isomorphism, i.e. (σ, ∇)-modules over A†_K, and the equivalence is functorial in A by mw-pullback-realises-frame-pullback.
hypotheses: Frobenius is an isomorphism Φ: F^*M → M; a mere horizontal map would not suffice for the radius-extension argument.
No condition on ∇ beyond integrability is assumed: convergence near the diagonal and then overconvergence are both consequences.
proofSteps: Localise on X (overconvergence is local, overconvergence-is-a-property (d)) so that Ω^1_{A†} is free on dz_1, …, dz_m; with F(z_i) = z_i^q + π g_i one has dF(dz_i) ∈ π Ω^1. If the connection matrices on generators have entries in π^{−r} A†, the matrices for the generators 1 ⊗ e_i of F^*M have entries in π^{−r+1} A†; transporting by Φ and iterating gives generators whose connection matrices have entries in A† (Berthelot 96-03, proof of (2.5.7), pp. 86–87).

With integral connection matrices, for every ρ > 1 there is η_0 > 1 with ‖∂^k e‖_{η_0} ≤ ρ^{|k|} ‖e‖_{η_0} (norm estimates of mw-pullback-realises-frame-pullback); choosing λ_0′ < p^{−1/(p−1)}/ρ gives convergence of the Taylor series on V_{λ_0 η_0} = {|τ_j| ≤ λ_0} ∩ U′_{η_0} (taylor-series-convergence-criterion).

Dwork's trick: with |π| < ϱ < 1 set λ_{n+1} = min(λ_n^{1/q}, λ_n/ϱ) → 1; choose η_{n+1} so that F × F maps V_{λ_{n+1} η_{n+1}} into V_{λ_n η_n} (using F(t_j) = t_j^q + π a_j and (F ⊗ F)(τ_j) = τ_j^q + π γ_j with γ_j in the diagonal ideal); extend ε inductively by p_1^*(Φ) ∘ (F×F)^*(ε) ∘ p_2^*(Φ)^{−1}, the extensions agreeing on overlaps because Φ is horizontal. The union of the V_{λ_n η_n} is a strict neighbourhood of the diagonal tube ((2.5.7), pp. 87–89).
The corollary combines this with affine-frame-global-sections-equivalence (iii) and the functoriality of mw-pullback-realises-frame-pullback ((2.5.8), p. 89).
acceptance: Dwork F-isocrystal: on A^1 with K = ℚ_p(π), σ = id, F(t) = t^p, the module (K⟨t⟩†, ∇(1) = −π dt) with Φ = multiplication by exp π(t − t^p) (a series of radius p^{(p−1)/p²} > 1) is a (σ,∇)-module, hence an overconvergent F-isocrystal (Berthelot (2.3.8)(ii)).

Kummer: on G_m with F(t) = t^p, the rank-one module with ∇(1) = a dt/t has a Frobenius structure if and only if a = m/(p − 1) with m ∈ ℤ, given by multiplication by t^m (Berthelot (2.3.8)(iii)); it is overconvergent for every a ∈ ℤ_p, so Frobenius is sufficient but not necessary for overconvergence.
Non-example: (K⟨t⟩†, ∇(1) = −dt) admits no Frobenius structure, consistently with its failure to be even convergent.

nodes.title: Étale maps of smooth affines lift uniquely to weak completions, with Frobenius and differentials
nodes.statement: Let A_0 be a smooth k-algebra with a smooth lift A and weak completion A†, and A_0 → B_0 an étale morphism. (a) There is an étale A†-algebra B lifting B_0, unique up to unique isomorphism, whose weak completion B† is flat and formally étale over A† for the π-adic topology, with Ω^1_{A†} ⊗_{A†} B† ≅ Ω^1_{B†} and Ω^1_{A†} ⊗ B̂ ≅ Ω^1_{B̂}. (b) A Frobenius lift F_{A†} over σ extends uniquely to a Frobenius lift F_{B†} compatible with it: the relative Frobenius B_0 ⊗_{A_0, F} A_0 → B_0 is an isomorphism and lifts uniquely to B† ⊗_{A†, F} A† ≅ B†. (c) If A_0 → B_0 is finite étale of constant degree d, then A†_K → B†_K is finite étale, B†_K is a projective A†_K-module of rank d with a trace map Tr: B†_K → A†_K satisfying Tr ∘ (inclusion) = d, and B†_K ⊗ Ω^i_{A†_K} ≅ Ω^i_{B†_K} for all i.
hypotheses: Étale lifts are unique by topological invariance of the étale site along the π-adic filtration; the lift of a Frobenius is unique only once F_{A†} is fixed.
proofSteps: (a): lift B_0 to an étale A†-algebra (weak-completion-henselian-descent (2); Étesse 2002, (1.2.2), citing his Padova paper, Théorème 4) and take its weak completion; flatness and the differential isomorphisms are Étesse's Proposition 1 (ii)(1)–(4), pp. 579–580, using formal étaleness and faithful flatness of A† → Â.

(b): the relative Frobenius of an étale morphism in characteristic p is an isomorphism; it lifts uniquely along the henselian pair by uniqueness of étale lifts, and F_{B†} is 1_{B†} ⊗ F_{A†} composed with that isomorphism (Étesse (1.2.2), pp. 578–579).

(c): for B_0 finite étale over A_0 the lift is finite étale over A†, hence B†_K is finite projective over A†_K with the trace of a finite étale algebra; the differential isomorphism in all degrees is Kedlaya, Finiteness, Proposition 3.4.5.
acceptance: Kummer cover: for p ∤ N, A_0 = k[t, t^{−1}] → B_0 = k[s, s^{−1}], t ↦ s^N, lifts to O[t, t^{−1}]† → O[s, s^{−1}]†, of degree N; the Frobenius t ↦ t^p extends to s ↦ s^p.
Degenerate case: B_0 = A_0 gives B† = A†.

Artin–Schreier: for the finite étale cover s^p − s = t of A^1_k, O[t]†[s]/(s^p − s − t) is an étale lift (the derivative p s^{p−1} − 1 is a unit), and by uniqueness every étale lift is isomorphic to it over O[t]†.
Non-example: for p odd the ramified cover t ↦ s² of A^1_k is not étale, and its lift O[t]†[s]/(s² − t) is not étale at s = 0; the lemma needs A_0 → B_0 étale.

nodes.title: Convergent isocrystals Isoc(X/K)
nodes.statement: Let X be a k-scheme of finite type. The category Isoc(X/K) of convergent isocrystals is the case Y = X of Isoc(X, Y/K) (isocrystals-glued-from-local-frames): when X is a closed subscheme of a formal O-scheme P smooth near X, its objects are coherent O_{]X[_P}-modules E with an integrable connection ∇ that is convergent, i.e. the Taylor isomorphisms extend to an isomorphism ε: p_2^*E ≅ p_1^*E on the whole tube ]X[_{P×P}; in general it is obtained by gluing. Equivalently (taylor-series-convergence-criterion with Z = ∅), for P affine with coordinates t_1, …, t_m near X, ‖∂^{[k]} e‖ λ^{|k|} → 0 for every λ < 1 and every section e over the closed tube [X]_λ. For X smooth affine with a smooth formal lift 𝔛 = Spf R over O (so ]X[_𝔛 = 𝔛_K), the objects are vector bundles on 𝔛_K with integrable connection such that lim_{|α|→∞} ‖θ^α(e)/α!‖ η^{|α|} = 0 for all 0 ≤ η < 1 and all sections e, θ_i being the components of ∇ in a framing. The category does not depend on P up to canonical equivalence, its objects are locally free, and for X proper over k it coincides with Isoc†(X/K).
hypotheses: K is complete discretely valued of characteristic 0 with residue field k of characteristic p; no Frobenius structure is assumed.
The convergence condition is on the whole tube ]X[_{P×P}, not on a strict neighbourhood of it; there is no boundary condition.
proofSteps: Independence of P is RD.3/independence-of-frame with Y = X (Berthelot 96-03 (2.3.1)–(2.3.2), pp. 68–70); the gluing and the Zariski stack property are isocrystals-glued-from-local-frames and zariski-stack-of-overconvergent-isocrystals (b).

The coordinate description is taylor-series-convergence-criterion with Z = ∅ ((2.2.14), p. 66); it agrees with Guo–Reinecke's Definition 2.12 on affine smooth formal lifts, and with Ogus's convergent isocrystals by Berthelot (2.3.4) (the tubes [X]_{P, p^{1/n}} are the generic fibres of Ogus's formal models T_{P,n}(X)).
acceptance: Dwork on A^1: (K⟨t⟩, ∇(1) = −π dt) is convergent (|π^k/k!| ≤ 1); (K⟨t⟩, ∇(1) = −dt) is not.
For X proper, Isoc(X/K) = Isoc†(X/K) by definition (Berthelot (2.3.9)).

sources.match: Defines convergent connections as those whose Taylor isomorphism extends to the whole tube of the diagonal, gives the coordinate criterion, defines the category of convergent isocrystals as the case of empty overconvergence locus, compares it with Ogus's definition, and notes that it equals the overconvergent category for proper X.
Describes isocrystals on an affine smooth formal lift as modules with connection over R[1/p] and defines convergent connections by the decay condition on θ^α(e)/α! for every η < 1.

Defines convergent F-isocrystals on a smooth affine through a smooth formal lift, notes that coherent modules with connection are locally free, and that without Frobenius an extra convergence condition on the Taylor isomorphism must be imposed.

nodes.title: Convergent F-isocrystals F^a-Isoc(X/K)
nodes.statement: Fix an automorphism σ of K lifting the p^a-power Frobenius of k (a ≥ 1, q = p^a). For E ∈ Isoc(X/K) let F_σ^*E be the pullback along σ followed by the pullback along the q-power Frobenius of X (Berthelot (2.3.7)). A convergent F^a-isocrystal on X is a pair (E, Φ) with E ∈ Isoc(X/K) and Φ: F_σ^*E ≅ E an isomorphism in Isoc(X/K); morphisms are morphisms of isocrystals commuting with Φ. The category F^a-Isoc(X/K) is abelian with ⊗ and internal Hom (Φ_{Hom}(F^*f) = Φ_F ∘ F^*(f) ∘ Φ_E^{−1}), linear over the fixed field K^{σ}. The Tate twist E(n) multiplies Φ by q^{−n}. For X smooth affine with a smooth formal lift P = Spf R and a Frobenius lift σ_P over σ, F^a-Isoc(X/K) is equivalent to the category of vector bundles E on P_K with integrable connection and a horizontal isomorphism σ_P^*E ≅ E; the convergence of ∇ is then automatic. For a perfect point η: Spec Ω → X, the fibre functor η^* takes values in F^a-isocrystals over Ω: finite-dimensional K(Ω)-vector spaces with a σ^a-semilinear bijection, where K(Ω) = W(Ω)[1/p] ⊗ K over the Witt vectors of the residue field; for a = 1 and K = W(k)[1/p] these are the isocrystals of Mathlib's WittVector.Isocrystal over the perfect field Ω.
hypotheses: σ lifts the q-power Frobenius of k; the case a = 1, K = W(k)[1/p] with k perfect and σ the Witt-vector Frobenius is the one compared with Mathlib's point isocrystals.
For F^a-isocrystals the natural Tate twist uses q^{−1} = p^{−a}; Berthelot's (2.3.8)(i) is the case a = 1, multiplying Φ by p^{−1}.
proofSteps: F_σ^* is the composite of the base change along σ (a functor Isoc(X, Y/K) → Isoc(X^{(σ)}, Y^{(σ)}/K)) and the pullback along the relative Frobenius (X, Y) → (X^{(σ)}, Y^{(σ)}), using isocrystals-glued-from-local-frames (c) (Berthelot 96-03 (2.3.7), pp. 75–76).

The local description with a Frobenius lift is Kedlaya, Notes, Definition 2.1, and Guo–Reinecke's Remark 2.16; the convergence of the connection follows from the Frobenius structure by Dwork's trick (the convergent analogue of frobenius-structure-forces-overconvergence; Kedlaya, Notes, Remark 2.12; Guo–Reinecke, Construction 2.11 and the paragraph before Definition 2.12).

Fibres at perfect points: pull back along η and use that Isoc(Spec Ω/K(Ω)) is the category of K(Ω)-vector spaces (convergent-isocrystal, test point); the Frobenius becomes a σ^a-semilinear bijection (Kedlaya, Notes, Remark 2.10; D’Addezio §2.2).
acceptance: Tate object over F_p (K = ℚ_p, a = 1): O(1) is the unit with Φ = p^{−1}; its fibre at the point is the one-dimensional isocrystal with Φ x = p^{−1} σ(x), Mathlib's StandardOneDimIsocrystal of slope −1.
Dwork: (K⟨t⟩, ∇(1) = −π dt, Φ = exp π(t − t^p)) on A^1 with σ_P(t) = t^p is a convergent F-isocrystal (it is even overconvergent).

nodes.title: Dwork's construction: the convergent F-isocrystal M^an of an F-crystal
nodes.statement: Assume O is a complete discrete valuation ring of mixed characteristic with ramification index e ≤ p − 1 and a Frobenius lift σ. Let X be a k-scheme of finite type and (M, Φ) a non-degenerate F-crystal on X/(O, σ) (a crystal of finite type with Φ: F^*M → M and V: M → F^*M, V∘Φ = p^n, Φ∘V = p^n for some n). Then there is a convergent F-isocrystal M^an on X/(K, σ), functorial in (M, Φ) and in X, constructed in two steps: (i) for a closed immersion X → P = Spf A into a smooth formal scheme, the completed divided-power envelope D̂ of the ideal of X maps to the algebra of the affinoid [X]_{P,|π|} by f^{[q]} ↦ π^{|q|} T^q/q!, which is bounded because e ≤ p − 1; this turns M into a coherent module M_P on [X]_{P,|π|} with a Taylor isomorphism on [X]_{P²,|π|} (an isocrystal convergent of radius |π|); (ii) a Frobenius lift F on P maps [X]_{P,λ_{n+1}} into [X]_{P,λ_n} for λ_n = |π|^{p^{−n}}, and the isomorphisms (F_K^*)^n(Φ ⊗ K) extend M_P and its Taylor isomorphism successively to ]X[_P = ⋃ [X]_{P,λ_n} and ]X[_{P²}.
hypotheses: e ≤ p − 1 is needed in step (i): the elements π^{|q|}/q! must be p-adic integers.
Non-degeneracy (existence of V) makes Φ ⊗ K an isomorphism, which step (ii) needs.
proofSteps: Glue from affine P (the construction is functorial); identify M with a separated complete D̂-module with stratification (Berthelot 96-03 (2.4.1), pp. 78–79).

Step (i): the composite D → A ⊗ K → (A ⊗ K){T}/(f_i − πT_i) is continuous for the π-adic topology since π^{q_1+…+q_r}/q_1!⋯q_r! ∈ ℤ_p when e ≤ p − 1, so it extends to D̂; base change gives M_P and, from the stratification, its Taylor isomorphism ((2.4.1.1)–(2.4.1.2)).

Step (ii): F_K maps [X]_{λ_{n+1}} into [X]_{λ_n} because F^*(f_i) = f_i^p + π g_i ((2.4.1.3)); setting M_n = (F_K^*)^n M_0 on [X]_{λ_n}, the maps (F_K^*)^n(Φ) identify M_n with the restriction of M_{n+1}, and the compatibility of Φ with the stratification extends the Taylor isomorphism to ]X[_{P²}.
acceptance: The unit crystal O_{X/O} with Φ = id gives the unit object (O_{]X[}, d, id).

Point: X = Spec k (k perfect, O = W(k)): an F-crystal is a Dieudonné-type module (W(k)^r, Φ) and M^an is (K^r, Φ ⊗ K); for (W(k), p^m σ) with m ≥ 0 one gets Mathlib's StandardOneDimIsocrystal of slope m.

Notes that the boundedness of p^n/n! uses the ramification bound and fails when the ramification index is at least p.

nodes.title: Convergent F-isocrystals are F-crystals up to isogeny and twist (Berthelot, Ogus)
nodes.statement: Let O be a complete discrete valuation ring of mixed characteristic with e ≤ p − 1 and Frobenius lift σ, and X a k-scheme of finite type. (a) The functor M ↦ M^an of f-crystal-to-convergent-f-isocrystal is fully faithful on non-degenerate F-crystals up to isogeny: Hom(M, N) ⊗ ℚ ≅ Hom(M^an, N^an). (b) If X is smooth over k, every convergent F-isocrystal N is isomorphic to M^an(n) for a non-degenerate F-crystal M (which may be taken p-torsion free) and an integer n ≥ 0. (c) Hence, for k perfect, O = W(k) and X smooth, the category F^a-Isoc(X/K) is equivalent to the category of pairs (E, Φ) with E an object of Isoc(X/W) = Crys(X/W) ⊗ ℚ (crystals of finite type up to isogeny) and Φ: (F^a)^*E ≅ E. (d) Locally, for 𝔛 = Spf R affine smooth over W(k) with special fibre 𝔛_s and a Frobenius lift F, the functor E ↦ E(𝔛)[1/p] = lim_r E(𝔛_s, 𝔛 ⊗ W_r)[1/p] is an equivalence from F-isocrystals on 𝔛_s/W(k) (crystalline) to vector bundles on 𝔛_η with flat convergent connection and horizontal Frobenius F^*E ≅ E. (e) The F-isocrystals on 𝔛_s for the crystalline site, on the crystalline site of 𝔛 ⊗ O_K/p, and on Ogus's convergent site of 𝔛 ⊗ O_K/p over W(k) are equivalent for a smooth formal O_K-scheme 𝔛 (any ramification), the inverses being restrictions.
hypotheses: (b) needs X smooth; the twist n is needed (the Tate object O(1) is not of the form M^an).
(c)–(e) use the unramified base W(k); the ramified case is reached through (e) and underlying-bundle-of-convergent-isocrystal.

Kedlaya states Theorem 2.2 for the absolute Frobenius (a = 1, k perfect, K = W(k)[1/p], X smooth); D’Addezio (§2.2) uses the equivalence for F^n-structures. Berthelot's argument in (2.4.1)–(2.4.2) applies with F replaced by F^a: the radii |π|^{q^{−n}}, q = p^a, still tend to 1, and Ogus's input in (b) does not involve the Frobenius.
proofSteps: (a): by internal Hom, compare Frobenius-invariant horizontal sections; locally with a Frobenius lift, sections of M^an on ]X[ are compatible families over the tubes [X]_{λ_n}, and the map B_1 → D̂ ⊗ ℚ sending T_i to (π^{−1} p!) f_i^{[p]} produces an inverse to the natural map from (M ⊗ ℚ)^{∇=0, Φ=1} (Berthelot 96-03 (2.4.2), first part, pp. 79–81).

(b): by (a) the statement is local, so assume X affine with a smooth lift; Ogus's Proposition 7.3 in 'The convergent topos in characteristic p' gives a crystal M, p-torsion free, with N ≅ M ⊗ ℚ compatibly with the Taylor isomorphisms, and p^n Φ is then an F-crystal structure ((2.4.2), second part, p. 81) — Ogus's proposition is an imported, unread input (gap).

(c) is (a) and (b) together, as stated by Kedlaya (Notes, Theorem 2.2, attributing full faithfulness to Ogus 1984 and essential surjectivity to Berthelot's (2.4.2)) and used by D’Addezio (§2.2, footnote 2).

(d) is the local form (Guo–Reinecke, Theorem 2.14, citing Berthelot's (2.4.2); Construction 2.11 identifies crystals with modules with quasi-nilpotent connection, CrystallineCohomology:CR.1/taylor-equivalence); (e) is Guo–Reinecke's Remark 2.15, citing Ogus 1984 (Example 2.7.3, Proposition 2.18) for the extension along the convergent site by Dwork's trick (imported, unread input).
acceptance: Point: for X = Spec k with k perfect, (c) says that F-isocrystals are Dieudonné modules up to isogeny, i.e. Mathlib's isocrystals over k.
Twist needed: O(1) (Φ = p^{−1}) is not M^an for any F-crystal M, because Φ would have to map a lattice into itself; it is M^an(1) for M the unit F-crystal.
Without Frobenius a crystal yields only an isocrystal convergent on the tube of radius |π| (Berthelot (2.4.1)(i)); the full convergence in (d) uses Frobenius.

nodes.title: The underlying vector bundle with connection of a convergent isocrystal on a smooth formal O_K-scheme
nodes.statement: Let 𝔛 be a smooth formal scheme over Spf O_K, O_K possibly ramified over W(k), with special fibre 𝔛_s and rigid generic fibre 𝔛_η, and let E be a convergent isocrystal on 𝔛_s/K_0, K_0 = W(k)[1/p]. (i) E has an underlying vector bundle with flat connection (E, ∇) on 𝔛_η: the realisation of E on the (not necessarily W(k)-smooth) formal scheme 𝔛, in which 𝔛_s is defined by an ideal of definition (isocrystals-glued-from-local-frames (b)); the connection is relative to K_0, equivalently to K. (ii) If E underlies a crystalline F-isocrystal on 𝔛_s/W(k), then for every W(k)-model Ũ of an affine open U ⊆ 𝔛 (Ũ ⊗_{W(k)} O_K ≅ U; such models exist for framed affines), (E, ∇)|_{U_η} ≅ (E(Ũ), ∇_Ũ) ⊗_{K_0} K, the right side being given by convergent-f-isocrystals-are-crystalline (d). The construction is exact, compatible with ⊗, duals and pullback along morphisms of smooth formal O_K-schemes.
hypotheses: Over a ramified base 𝔛 has no Frobenius lift compatible with a lift of Frobenius on O_K in general; Frobenius structures are carried by E on the special fibre, not by the bundle.
Framings (étale maps to Spf O_K⟨x_1^{±1}, …, x_d^{±1}⟩) exist on a basis of affine opens (Guo–Reinecke, Lemma 2.10).

Guo–Reinecke state (i) for convergent isocrystals on Ogus's convergent site of 𝔛_{p=0}; by Berthelot (2.3.4) these are the convergent isocrystals defined by tubes, and tubes depend only on the reduced subscheme, so a convergent isocrystal on 𝔛_s is the same datum.
proofSteps: Realisation: for an affine open U with a closed immersion of U_s into a smooth formal W(k)-scheme P, lift U_s → P to u: U → P by formal smoothness along the ideal of definition, and put E_U = u_K^* E_P on U_η = ]U_s[_U; independence and gluing are isocrystals-glued-from-local-frames (b) (Berthelot 96-03 (2.3.2)(ii), last paragraph, pp. 70–71).

(ii): for a framed affine U, the unique W(k)-model Ũ with lifted framing (Guo–Reinecke, Lemma 2.9) gives u: U = Ũ ⊗ O_K → Ũ, so E_U = (E(Ũ)[1/p]) ⊗_{K_0} K with its connection (Guo–Reinecke, Proposition 2.17, citing Ogus 1984, Remark 2.8.1, Theorem 2.15, Proposition 2.21).
acceptance: Unit: the underlying bundle of the unit isocrystal is (O_{𝔛_η}, d).
Unramified case: O_K = W(k) and 𝔛 = Ũ give E(𝔛)[1/p] itself.

nodes.title: Unit-root F-isocrystals
nodes.statement: Let E be a convergent or overconvergent F^a-isocrystal on X. E is unit-root if for every geometric point x̄ of X all Frobenius slopes of the fibre x̄^*E are zero, i.e. the fibre has a basis e_1, …, e_r with Φ(e_i ⊗ 1) = e_i (Étesse §5.1); equivalently the fibre at every perfect point is isoclinic of slope 0. Unit-root objects form a full subcategory F^a-Isoc(X/K)^0 (respectively F^a-Isoc†(X/K)^0) stable under ⊗, duals, subquotients and extensions, with no non-zero morphisms to or from isoclinic objects of non-zero slope. At a perfect point with a = 1 and K = W(k)[1/p], unit-root means that the Mathlib isocrystal has a W-lattice L with Φ(L) = L, equivalently a basis in which the matrix of Φ lies in GL_r(W).
hypotheses: Slopes are computed after pulling back to a perfect (or algebraically closed) point, where the Dieudonné–Manin classification applies.
For overconvergent objects the condition is on the image in the convergent category; it is the same pointwise condition.
proofSteps: Fibres at perfect points are F^a-isocrystals over K(Ω) (convergent-f-isocrystal); over an algebraically closed point Dieudonné–Manin (CrystallineCohomology:CR.4/isocrystal-slope-decomposition; Mathlib's isocrystal_classification in rank one) decomposes them by slope, and slope 0 means a Φ-fixed basis (Étesse 2002 §5.1, p. 590; Kedlaya, Notes, Definition 3.3, p. 6).

Stability under subquotients and extensions and the vanishing of Hom between distinct slopes are Kedlaya, Notes, Definition 3.3 and the remark after it (slopes are additive in exact sequences); the lattice characterisation at a point follows from Dieudonné–Manin.
acceptance: The Dwork F-isocrystal L_π (∇(1) = −π dt, Φ = θ(t) := exp π(t − t^p), σ = id) is unit-root: it has rank one, hence is isoclinic (Kedlaya, Notes, Remark 3.5), and at the point 0 its Frobenius is θ(0) = 1. At the other F_p-points the Frobenius is not 1: by Dwork's theorem θ(1) = ζ_p is a primitive p-th root of unity (ζ_p ≡ 1 + π mod π²) and θ(x̂) = ζ_p^x for the Teichmüller lift x̂ of x ∈ F_p, a unit, consistently with slope 0. The tempting substitution x̂^p = x̂ inside exp π(t − t^p) is not legitimate: exp(πt) and exp(−πt^p) diverge on |t| = 1, and only their product θ converges there.
The Tate object O(1) is isoclinic of slope −1, hence not unit-root.

nodes.title: Katz–Crew: unit-root F-isocrystals are lisse p-adic sheaves
nodes.statement: Let k be a perfect field containing F_q (q = p^a), K = W(k)[1/p] with σ the Witt-vector Frobenius, and X a smooth separated k-scheme of finite type. Let ℚ_q = W(F_q)[1/p] ⊆ K. The functor V ↦ (V ⊗_{ℚ_q} O_{X/K}, 1 ⊗ σ^a) is an exact fully faithful ⊗-functor from the category of étale ℚ_q-local systems on X to F^a-Isoc(X/K), with essential image the unit-root convergent F^a-isocrystals; a quasi-inverse sends E to the étale sheaf of Φ-fixed horizontal sections. If X is connected with a geometric point x̄, unit-root convergent F^a-isocrystals are thus equivalent to continuous representations of π_1^ét(X, x̄) on finite-dimensional ℚ_q-vector spaces. For a = 1 this is the equivalence of Kedlaya, Notes, Theorem 3.7; the version with ℚ_q-coefficients and F^a-structures is the one used in D’Addezio, proof of Proposition 3.3.4.
hypotheses: X smooth; the field k perfect and containing F_q so that the F^a-isocrystal category is ℚ_q-linear.

Local systems are étale ℚ_q-local systems: the étale stackification of the isogeny category of ℤ_q-local systems (InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups:IG.0/adic-local-systems, with W(F_q)-coefficients).
proofSteps: Lattices: a unit-root convergent F^a-isocrystal is, locally on X, M ⊗ ℚ for a crystal M of finite locally free modules with Φ: (F^a)^*M ≅ M an isomorphism (Kedlaya, Notes, Remark 2.3 records that unit-root objects come from crystals of locally free modules; for the convergent/crystalline translation use convergent-f-isocrystals-are-crystalline (c)).

Katz's construction (the proof in Crew 1987, Theorem 2.1, and Katz's Proposition 4.1.1 are not publicly accessible; this outline is supplied here): on M/p^m the equation Φ(v) = v is solved étale-locally, because the Lang map g ↦ g^{−1} σ^a(g) on GL_r(W_m(k′)) is finite étale and surjective; the solutions form a locally constant sheaf T_m of free W_m(F_q)-modules of rank r, and T = lim T_m is a ℤ_q-local system with M ≅ T ⊗ O_crys compatibly with Φ = 1 ⊗ σ^a.

Conversely T ↦ T ⊗ O_crys with Φ = 1 ⊗ σ^a is a unit-root F^a-crystal; on Hom-spaces both constructions identify Hom(V, V′) with the Φ-fixed horizontal sections of the internal Hom, which gives full faithfulness; pass to isogeny categories and stackify on both sides (rational local systems are étale-locally of the form T[1/p]), using that convergent F^a-isocrystals on smooth X form an étale stack (Kedlaya, Notes, Definition 2.1 and the remark after it).
For X connected, the étale ℚ_q-local systems are continuous ℚ_q-representations of π_1^ét(X, x̄) (IG.0/adic-local-systems with IG.0/etale-fundamental-group).
acceptance: Point over F_p: the F-isocrystal (ℚ_p, Φ = u) with u ∈ ℤ_p^× is unit-root and corresponds to the character of Gal(F̄_p/F_p) sending the arithmetic Frobenius to u^{−1}: a Φ-fixed vector v of K̂^{ur} satisfies u σ(v) = v, so σ(v) = u^{−1} v.
Non-example: (ℚ_p, Φ = p) over F_p has no non-zero Φ-fixed vector over K̂^{ur} (v_p(p σ(v)) = 1 + v_p(v)), consistently with its slope 1.
Over an algebraically closed point the theorem is Dieudonné–Manin: unit-root F-isocrystals are ℚ_p-vector spaces tensored with K.

nodes.title: Étesse: convergent direct summands of overconvergent F-isocrystals are overconvergent
nodes.statement: Let X be a smooth separated k-scheme of finite type. (1) If E ∈ F^a-Isoc†(X/K) and its image Ê ∈ F^a-Isoc(X/K) decomposes as Ê ≅ E_1 ⊕ E_2, then there are E_1†, E_2† ∈ F^a-Isoc†(X/K), unique up to isomorphism, with Ê_i† ≅ E_i and E ≅ E_1† ⊕ E_2†. (2) If E ≅ E_1† ⊕ E_2† and E′ ≅ E′_1† ⊕ E′_2† are two such objects and g: E → E′ is a morphism whose image ĝ is diagonal, ĝ = φ ⊕ ψ, then there are unique f_i: E_i† → E′_i† with g = f_1 ⊕ f_2 and ĝ = f̂_1 ⊕ f̂_2.
hypotheses: X smooth; Frobenius structures are part of the data (the proof uses the Monsky–Washnitzer description of frobenius-structure-forces-overconvergence).
proofSteps: Localise on X (Zariski stack, zariski-stack-of-overconvergent-isocrystals), so X = Spec A_0 smooth affine with lift A and Frobenius lift F on A†; by frobenius-structure-forces-overconvergence, E is a (σ,∇)-module N over A†_K and Ê corresponds to N ⊗ Â_K (Étesse 2002, §5.2, pp. 591–592).

Since (A†, πA†) is a henselian pair and A† is a Zariski ring (weak-completion-henselian-descent), finitely generated projective Â_K-modules descend uniquely to A†_K and summands of N ⊗ Â_K lift to summands M, P of N (Étesse, Proposition 6 and Corollaries 1–2, p. 586, by Elkik's approximation theorem); the decomposition is identified as M = M̂ ∩ N inside N ⊗ Â_K using A†_K = Â_K ∩ B for suitable faithfully flat extensions (Proposition 2 and its corollary, pp. 580–583).

The connection and Frobenius of N restrict to M because Ω^1 and the Frobenius pullbacks are compatible with these intersections (Corollary 2 (2)(iii)–(iv) and Propositions 9′ and 10′, pp. 590–592); this gives the affine case of (1) and (2), and the pieces glue by the Zariski stack property (Théorème 6 and its proof, p. 598).
acceptance: Degenerate splitting: Ê = Ê ⊕ 0 lifts to E ⊕ 0.
Kummer pair (p odd, X = G_m): the direct sum of the Kummer F-isocrystals with a = 0 and a = 1/(p−1) is overconvergent, and its convergent decomposition lifts to the overconvergent decomposition.

Non-example: a convergent subobject that is not a direct summand need not be overconvergent — the unit-root subobject of H^1 of the universal elliptic curve on the ordinary locus (RD.3/punctured-curve-boundary-acceptance; Berthelot (2.3.9)(iii)).

sources.locator: Théorème 6 and its proof, p. 598; Proposition 6 with Corollaries 1–2, p. 586; Propositions 9′ and 10′, pp. 590–592

nodes.title: Étesse: étale descent for overconvergent F-isocrystals
nodes.statement: Let X be a smooth separated k-scheme of finite type. (1) Every étale surjective morphism f: Y → X satisfies descent for overconvergent F^a-isocrystals: f^* induces an equivalence from F^a-Isoc†(X/K) to the category of objects of F^a-Isoc†(Y/K) with descent data relative to f (isomorphisms p_2^*E ≅ p_1^*E on Y ×_X Y satisfying the cocycle condition on Y ×_X Y ×_X Y). (2) If f: Y → X is étale, dominant and separated, F^a-Isoc†(X/K) is the 2-fibre product of F^a-Isoc(X/K) and F^a-Isoc†(Y/K) over F^a-Isoc(Y/K): a convergent F^a-isocrystal on X whose pullback to Y is overconvergent is overconvergent, uniquely, and similarly for morphisms. (3) The analogous fibre-product statements hold for an extension of the base field k ⊆ k′ (with K ⊆ K′ as in Étesse 1.1) and for the combination of both. (4) A proper surjective generically étale morphism f: Y → X also satisfies descent for overconvergent F^a-isocrystals.
hypotheses: X smooth and Frobenius structures present; the convergent descent results of Ogus (1984, Theorems 4.5 and 4.6) are used over a perfect closure of k.
proofSteps: Base change to an algebraic closure k′ of k: by Ogus's theorem the convergent F^a-isocrystal descends along f′ (imported, unread input) (Étesse 2002, proof of Théorème 1, p. 593).

nodes.title: Monsky–Washnitzer algebras are henselian along π; lifting of étale algebras and descent of projective modules
nodes.statement: Let A be a finitely generated O-algebra (O a complete discrete valuation ring with uniformiser π) with weak completion A†, π-adic completion Â, and A_0 = A/πA. (1) (Spec A†, Spec A_0) is a henselian pair, and A† → Â is faithfully flat and formally étale for the π-adic topology. (2) Every smooth (respectively étale, finite étale) A_0-algebra B_0 lifts to a smooth (respectively étale, finite étale) A†-algebra B, and sections lift. (3) Every finitely generated projective Â_K-module (Â_K = Â ⊗ K) is isomorphic to M ⊗_{A†_K} Â_K for a finitely generated projective A†_K-module M, and two such M with isomorphic base changes are isomorphic.
hypotheses: A† is weakly complete of finite type (always the case for the weak completion of a finitely generated algebra); A is Noetherian.
proofSteps: (1): A† is Noetherian with π in its radical and A† → Â is faithfully flat (Monsky–Washnitzer); A†/π^n = Â/π^n gives formal étaleness; for a finite A†-algebra B, idempotents of B/πB lift to B because they lift to B̂ and B → B̂ is faithfully flat with B weakly complete (Monsky–Washnitzer, Theorem 3.8), which is the henselian property (Étesse, Padova 2002, Proposition 2 and Théorème 3, pp. 113–115).

(2): Elkik, Théorème 6, p. 580: over a noetherian henselian pair (A, J) every smooth A/J-algebra lifts to a smooth A-algebra; the proof reduces to relative complete intersections through the symmetric algebra of the conormal module and lifts sections over the henselian pair (SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.0/henselian-smooth-lifting). Applied to (A†, πA†), which is noetherian and henselian by (1), it gives the smooth case; the étale and finite étale refinements and the lifting of sections are Étesse, Padova 2002, Théorème 4, pp. 116–117, whose proof cites Elkik's Théorème 6 (finite étale algebras also follow from SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.0/henselian-finite-etale-equivalence).

(3): Elkik's Théorème 3 (p. 569): over a henselian pair (A, J), a finitely generated Â-module locally free outside V(J) comes from a finitely generated A-module locally free outside V(J); Corollaire 1 and the following Lemme (p. 573) give the statement for locally free modules on Spec Â ∖ V(J) and uniqueness of isomorphism classes. With J = πA† this is (3) (Étesse 2002, Proposition 6 and Corollaire 1, p. 586).
acceptance: A = O[t]: A† = O⟨t⟩†, and a projective K⟨t⟩-module of rank one (necessarily free, K⟨t⟩ being a principal ideal domain) descends to the free module of rank one over K⟨t⟩†.

Henselian property on a finite étale algebra: for p odd, the idempotents of O⟨t⟩†[s]/(s² − (1 + πt)) modulo π (where the algebra splits as k[t] × k[t]) lift to idempotents, since 1 + πt has a square root in O⟨t⟩† given by the binomial series.
Non-example: the polynomial ring O[t] itself is not henselian along π: 1 + πt has no square root in O[t].

nodes.title: Kummer isocrystals K_a on G_m
nodes.statement: On the frame (G_m, P^1_k, P̂^1_O) with coordinate t, for a ∈ ℤ_p let K_a be the free j†O_{P^1_K}-module of rank one on a generator e with ∇(e) = a e ⊗ dt/t. Global sections of j†O are the Laurent series Σ_{n∈ℤ} c_n t^n converging on some annulus ρ < |t| < 1/ρ, ρ < 1 (written K⟨t, t^{−1}⟩†), and the sections on the tube ]G_m[ = {|t| = 1} form K⟨t, t^{−1}⟩. Then: K_a is an overconvergent isocrystal on G_m; K_a ⊗ K_b ≅ K_{a+b} and K_a^∨ ≅ K_{−a}; K_a ≅ K_b if and only if a − b ∈ ℤ (an isomorphism K_b → K_a is e_b ↦ t^{b−a} e_a); the horizontal sections of K_a, over the tube or over a strict neighbourhood, are K·t^{−a} e if a ∈ ℤ and 0 otherwise; the pullback along t ↦ t^N is K_{Na}; and, for the Frobenius lift t ↦ t^p with σ = id on K, K_a admits a Frobenius structure if and only if (p − 1)a ∈ ℤ, the structure being multiplication by t^{(p−1)a}.
hypotheses: a ∈ ℤ_p is needed for convergence: for a ∉ ℤ_p the binomial coefficients binom(a, k) are unbounded and the connection is not even convergent.
Frobenius structures are taken with σ = id on K (K ⊇ ℚ_p arbitrary) and the lift t ↦ t^p.
proofSteps: Overconvergence: by taylor-series-convergence-criterion on the two affine charts (overconvergence is local on P, overconvergence-is-a-property (d)), ∂^{[k]} e = binom(a, k) t^{−k} e with |binom(a, k)| ≤ 1, so on {η ≤ |t| ≤ 1/η} the decay ‖∂^{[k]}e‖ λ^k ≤ (λ/η)^k → 0 holds for η > λ; the chart at ∞ is the same with −a.

Tensor, dual and pullback are computed on generators; an isomorphism K_b → K_a sends e_b to g e_a with t g′ = (b − a) g, so g = c t^{b−a}, a unit of K⟨t, t^{−1}⟩† exactly when a − b ∈ ℤ; horizontal sections are the case b = 0, where the Laurent coefficients satisfy (n + a) g_n = 0.

Frobenius: a horizontal Φ: F^*K_a → K_a, F^*K_a having ∇(1) = pa dt/t, is multiplication by some h with t h′ = a(p − 1) h, so h = c t^{a(p−1)}, analytic and invertible on annuli near |t| = 1 iff a(p − 1) ∈ ℤ (Berthelot 96-03 (2.3.8)(iii)).
acceptance: K_0 is the unit; K_1 ≅ K_0 through e ↦ t e.
For p odd, K_{1/2} carries the Frobenius structure t^{(p−1)/2} (Kummer F-isocrystal of the double cover).

nodes.title: A p-adic Liouville-type exponent: p^n/(n + λ) tends to 0 but not geometrically
nodes.statement: There is λ ∈ ℤ_p ∖ ℤ such that the sequence f_n = p^n/(n + λ), n ≥ 1, satisfies |f_n| → 0 while for no ρ > 1 does |f_n| ρ^n → 0 (equivalently limsup |f_n|^{1/n} = 1). Explicitly one may take λ = −Σ_{k≥1} p^{m_k} with m_1 = 2, N_k = Σ_{j≤k} p^{m_j} and m_{k+1} = N_k − k; this λ is not rational. Consequently the power series Σ_{n≥1} f_n t^n lies in the Tate algebra K⟨t⟩ of the closed unit disc but not in its overconvergent subring K⟨t⟩† (nor in K⟨t, t^{−1}⟩†).
hypotheses: Any p ≥ 2; the choice of m_k only needs v_p(N_k + λ) − N_k → −∞ slowly enough that N_k ↦ v_p(N_k + λ)/N_k tends to 1.
proofSteps: The m_k increase strictly (m_2 = p² − 1 ≥ 3 and m_{k+1} ≥ p^{m_k} − k), and −λ has infinitely many non-zero and infinitely many zero p-adic digits, so λ ∉ ℤ and n + λ ≠ 0 for all n; since the gaps m_{k+1} − m_k tend to infinity, the digit expansion of −λ is not eventually periodic, so λ ∉ ℚ.
For n = N_k: N_k + λ = −Σ_{j>k} p^{m_j} has valuation m_{k+1} = N_k − k, so |f_{N_k}| = p^{−k} → 0 but |f_{N_k}| ρ^{N_k} = p^{−k} ρ^{N_k} → ∞ for every ρ > 1.

For N_k < n < N_{k+1} (with N_0 = 0): n + λ = (n − N_k) + (N_k + λ) with 0 < n − N_k < p^{m_{k+1}} ≤ p^{v_p(N_k+λ)}, so v_p(n + λ) = v_p(n − N_k) ≤ log_p n and |f_n| ≤ n p^{−n} → 0. This construction is supplied here; it realises the p-adic Liouville phenomenon referred to by Kedlaya (Notes, Remark 5.6).
acceptance: Contrast: for λ = −1/2 (p odd), v_p(n − 1/2) = v_p(2n − 1) ≤ log_p(2n), so |f_n| ≤ 2n p^{−n} and Σ f_n t^n converges for |t| < p: it is overconvergent. The numbers n − 1/2 are not all units (p divides 2n − 1 for n = (p + 1)/2); what matters is that v_p(n + λ) grows only logarithmically. In general Σ f_n t^n is overconvergent if and only if limsup_n v_p(n + λ)/n < 1, and no λ ∈ ℤ_p ∖ ℤ has |n + λ| bounded below, because ℕ is dense in ℤ_p.
Contrast: for λ ∈ ℤ the sequence is undefined at n = −λ, which is why λ ∉ ℤ is required.
